Calculate run expectancy added for verified events

Source: R/calculate_run_impact.R
calculate_run_impact.Rd

Apply a supplied reference matrix to verified base-out transitions. RE24 equals runs scored plus ending expectancy minus starting expectancy.

Usage

calculate_run_impact(plays, expectancy)

Arguments

plays

Data frame containing character game_id, event_id, player; integer-valued outs_before, bases_before, outs_after, bases_after, runs_scored; and logical verified. All events must be verified. Base masks use 1 for first, 2 for second and 4 for third, added together. Before outs must be 0:2, after outs 0:3, and base masks 0:7. Outs cannot decrease and runs scored must be nonnegative.

expectancy

Data frame with all 24 distinct combinations of outs (0:2) and bases (0:7), plus finite nonnegative numeric expected_runs.

Value

The input data frame with numeric re_before, re_after, and re24 columns. Three outs sets ending expectancy to zero. Empty input returns the same columns with zero rows. Sum re24 over the desired events.

Details

The caller chooses a documented reference matrix appropriate to the league and run environment. This function neither estimates that matrix nor infers runner movement. verified is a caller assertion, not automatic verification. Incomplete or assumed states must not be marked verified. Duplicate game/event IDs and invalid states are errors. Standalone runner events need the responsible runner in player; do not credit them to the batter. Walk-off states use the supplied base-out expectancy, not forced zero simply because the game ended. RE24 describes situational value, not a prediction or proof of clutch ability. Original columns are retained.

References

Weinberg, Neil. 2014. "RE24." FanGraphs, July 30. https://library.fangraphs.com/misc/re24/

See also

compare_personal_season()

Examples

# Fictional matrix for demonstrating the interface, not an MLB estimate.
reference <- expand.grid(outs = 0:2, bases = 0:7)
reference$expected_runs <- (3 - reference$outs) * 0.2 + reference$bases * 0.1
plays <- data.frame(game_id = "demo", event_id = "1", player = "Demo Batter",
  outs_before = 0, bases_before = 0, outs_after = 0, bases_after = 0,
  runs_scored = 1, verified = TRUE)
calculate_run_impact(plays, reference)$re24
#> [1] 1
